name: Nuxt 4 public-web rendering capabilities
description: Official Nuxt 4 rendering, prerendering and SEO metadata capabilities used to evaluate public-web architecture without treating framework adoption as an automatic SEO requirement.

rules.title: Recognize Nuxt universal rendering as an available capability
rules.summary: Nuxt 4 supports universal rendering that returns fully rendered HTML before hydration; this is a framework capability, not evidence that an existing application must migrate.

rules.title: Model route-specific rendering and cache strategies
rules.summary: Nuxt routeRules can select prerendering, SSR/client-only behavior, redirects and SWR/ISR-style caching per route class; audits should compare those capabilities to the target project's actual route/freshness needs.

rules.title: Do not assume crawl-based prerender discovers every dynamic route
rules.summary: Nuxt crawl-based prerender follows anchor links from discovered pages; unlinked or dynamic routes may require explicit prerender routes or another rendering strategy.

rules.title: Recognize Nuxt's server-compatible head and SEO metadata primitives
rules.summary: Nuxt uses Unhead and provides useHead/useSeoMeta for reactive page metadata; their availability reduces custom head plumbing but does not by itself improve search outcomes.

rules.title: Account for Cloudflare-compatible Nuxt edge deployment
rules.summary: Nuxt/Nitro supports edge-side rendering on Cloudflare Pages; migration analysis must still measure deployment complexity, runtime constraints and hydration behavior in the target environment.

rules.title: Require a measured capability or maintenance gap before recommending Nuxt migration
rules.summary: Do not recommend Nuxt solely because it offers SSR or SEO helpers. Compare response HTML completeness, dynamic freshness, cache/revalidation needs, route scale, build/runtime cost, operational complexity and migration blast radius against the existing architecture first.
